Let's start overseas.

A magnitude seven-point-seven earthquake struck off eastern Indonesia early Saturday, out near the island of Flores, and it's turned deadly — at least forty-seven people killed, and officials expect that to climb as they reach the worst-hit villages.

More than two hundred aftershocks rattled the region through the day, the strongest a six-point-two, and a second big quake hit off Sumatra.

A tsunami warning went up but was lifted within a few hours; the bigger damage is on land, with landslides cutting roads and around two thousand people evacuating.

Your science note today is a brain one, and a surprising one.

A big Stanford study found the aging brain isn't nearly as sealed off from the body as we thought — immune cells from the bloodstream start slipping into brain tissue as early as middle age.

It could reshape how we think about aging and neurodegeneration down the line.

Early work, more a new door than a treatment, but a genuinely eye-opening result.

It lifted off from Cape Canaveral just after four this morning your time, dropped a fresh batch of Globalstar satellites into orbit, and the booster flew itself home to land back at the Cape.

Clean and routine — nice one to have gone off without a hitch.

And to send you off a little smarter.

Word of the day: sloper — that rounded, holdless-feeling grip you can't crimp, so you paste your whole open hand over it and hang on with friction and body position, like palming a basketball.
